subject: Social Science
central_question: How can India identify, plan, use and conserve its varied land and soil resources so that development meets present needs without harming future generations?
in_scope_units: Meaning of a resource and the interdependent relationship among nature, technology, institutions and human beings
Classification of resources by origin, exhaustibility, ownership and status of development
Development of Resources, including depletion, unequal accumulation and ecological crises caused by indiscriminate use
Sustainable development, the Rio de Janeiro Earth Summit of 1992 and Agenda 21
Resource Planning and the need for balanced planning across regions of India
Resource Planning in India through inventory, suitable planning structures and integration with national plans
Conservation of Resources and major ideas associated with Gandhiji, the Club of Rome, Schumacher and the Brundtland Commission
Land Resources and India's major relief features
Land Utilisation categories and the meanings of net sown area and gross cropped area
Land Use Pattern in India and the physical and human factors that shape it
Land Degradation and Conservation Measures, including regional causes and remedies
Soil as a Resource, soil formation factors and the soil profile
Classification and distribution of alluvial, black, red and yellow, laterite, arid and forest soils
Soil Erosion and Soil Conservation through contour ploughing, terrace cultivation, strip cropping and shelter belts
End-of-chapter exercises, project work and resource-conservation activities
banned_topics: Detailed cropping seasons, major crops and farming systems, which belong to the Agriculture chapter
Detailed forest and wildlife biodiversity categories and conservation programmes, which belong to the Forest and Wildlife Resources chapter
Multipurpose river projects, dams and rainwater harvesting systems, which belong to the Water Resources chapter
Detailed extraction and distribution of minerals and energy sources, which belong to the Minerals and Energy Resources chapter
Industrial location and manufacturing-sector pollution, which belong to the Manufacturing Industries chapter

known_pitfalls.claim: Anything found in nature automatically becomes a resource.
known_pitfalls.correction: Something becomes a resource only when it can satisfy human needs and is technologically accessible, economically feasible and culturally acceptable.

known_pitfalls.claim: Resources are free gifts of nature and human beings only consume them.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter states that resources are a function of human activities; people use technology and institutions to transform materials from the environment into resources.

known_pitfalls.claim: Sustainable development means stopping development in order to protect nature.
known_pitfalls.correction: Sustainable development allows development, but it must not damage the environment or compromise the needs of future generations.

known_pitfalls.claim: A region will develop automatically if it has abundant natural resources.
known_pitfalls.correction: Resource availability must be supported by appropriate technology, skilled human resources and institutional changes; otherwise resource-rich regions may remain economically backward.

known_pitfalls.claim: Net sown area includes every field cultivated more than once during a year.
known_pitfalls.correction: Net sown area is the physical area on which crops are sown and harvested; net sown area plus the area sown more than once is the gross cropped area.

known_pitfalls.claim: Black soil is sandy and cannot retain moisture.
known_pitfalls.correction: Black or regur soil is extremely fine and clayey, has a high moisture-holding capacity and is ideal for cotton.

known_pitfalls.claim: Bangar is newer and more fertile than Khadar.
known_pitfalls.correction: Bangar is old alluvium with more kankar nodules, while Khadar is new alluvium with finer particles and greater fertility.

known_pitfalls.claim: Terrace cultivation and contour ploughing increase the speed of runoff on slopes.
known_pitfalls.correction: Both methods slow the movement of water down slopes and therefore help control soil erosion.

recommended_example_progression: Begin with NCERT Project/Activity 3: reason through how exhaustion of oil supplies would affect daily life and why non-renewable resources require conservation.
Use NCERT Exercise 3(ii): explain how technological and economic development can increase the transformation and consumption of resources.
Use NCERT Exercise 3(i): organise the categories and determinants of India's land-use pattern and connect them with the limited rise in forest area since 1960-61.
Use NCERT Exercise 2(ii): identify alluvial soil in the eastern coastal river deltas and justify the answer with three textbook features.
Conclude with NCERT Exercise 2(iii): select contour ploughing, terrace cultivation and related measures for controlling soil erosion in hilly areas.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter ends with EXERCISES 1-3 on page 11, followed by PROJECT/ACTIVITY items 1-4 and the resource-and-soil word puzzle continuing on page 12.
